title: Heaven comes down
hook: not escape to the clouds, but heaven and earth renewed

segments.voice: Yesterday, O death: Paul's taunt, borrowed from Hosea. Your line was where is your sting? Did you ask a fear that question? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

A cartoon in a magazine: a man in a white robe sits alone on a cloud, holding a harp, looking bored. The joke works because the picture is familiar. Heaven, in that picture, is somewhere up and away, thin and misty, where souls float off to after the body is done. The earth is left behind like an old coat. Now open the last pages of the Bible and watch which way things move. John doesn't see anyone floating up. He sees something coming down. The movement runs the other way from the cartoon, and that direction is the heart of today's word.
screen: `A MAN ON A CLOUD WITH A HARP.`

segments.voice: First, the direction. In Revelation, John writes, in the King James words: "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven." Down. God's home arrives on earth, and a voice says "the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them." The ending isn't people leaving the world. It's God moving in. Second, the prayer Christians already pray. In the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teaches, "Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven." Not take us out of the earth. Bring heaven's way into it. Third, creation waiting. Paul writes to Rome that "the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now," and he hopes that "the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption." Not only people. The whole created world, waiting to be set free. Isaiah had said it long before: "For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth." Fourth, the word. A couple of weeks ago this block heard Paul say that anyone in Christ "is a new creature." The Greek behind that, kainē ktisis, can just as well be translated new creation. The same hope runs from one person to the whole world: not thrown away, made new. Christians hold these pictures in different balances. Some speak mostly of heaven as where the faithful go at death. Others stress the hope that God will renew this earth itself. Some hold both together: rest with God now, and a renewed creation at the end. What the Bible's last pages add is the direction. Heaven comes down.
screen: `IN EARTH, AS IT IS IN HEAVEN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: care for a piece of the earth. Settle, and breathe. Notice what's right around you: the floor under your feet, the air, a plant, the view through a window. All of it, in this hope, is worth making new, not throwing away. Choose one small thing you can care for today: water a plant, pick up litter on your street, turn off something left running. If you pray, you can say the line from the Lord's Prayer: thy will be done in earth. If you don't, just let your attention rest on the ground under you. The bell holds the time.
New creation. The hope that God doesn't throw the world away but makes it new, heaven and earth renewed, God dwelling with people.
Your line: heaven comes down. Do the one small act of care you chose, for a plant, a street, a patch of ground, as if this earth is worth keeping. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Christians pray "thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven" in the Lord's Prayer, and some churches link the hope of a new creation with caring for the earth, through creation-care ministries or a season of prayer for creation.

original.note: Greek: new creation, or new creature, Paul's phrase in 2 Corinthians 5:17.

trapdoor: what you thought: heaven is up in the clouds, and earth gets left behind.
what it means: the Bible ends with the holy city coming down and God dwelling with people: heaven and earth renewed.
what a scholar hears: kainē ktisis, new creation, and Romans 8, where the whole creation waits to be freed from corruption.

notes: Angle chosen to avoid repeating days 1311–1314 (Revelation 21–22): today is about direction (down, not up), the Lord's Prayer and Romans 8.

The three ways Christians balance heaven-at-death and renewed earth are given without ranking. Some readers also cite 2 Peter 3:10–13 (the earth 'burned up', then 'new heavens and a new earth'); not used. Confirm fair.
'Isaiah had said it long before' is a relative time phrase, not a date.
howItsDone: 'a season of prayer for creation' refers to the Season of Creation kept by some churches; confirm wording.
Original: καινὴ κτίσις (2 Corinthians 5:17; also Galatians 6:15). Confirm.
